history: Created by Jörg Meyer at Le Lion in Hamburg in 2008. He posted it as the "Gin Pesto" and it spread through European bars within a year — one of the few genuinely modern drinks to reach classic status.
whyItWorks: Basil is bruised, not pulverised. Shaken hard with lemon it gives up its oils without the bitterness that comes from tearing the leaf.
steps: Put the basil leaves in the shaker with the lemon and syrup.
Muddle briefly — press the leaves, do not shred them.
Add the gin and ice, shake hard and short.
Double-strain over fresh cubed ice and crown with a basil top.
techniqueNotes: Over-muddling turns it bitter and grey. Three or four presses is enough.
Serve it fast — the green fades within a few minutes.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Citrus-forward and clean behind the basil.
Softer and more floral; a gentler smash.

substitutions.notes: Mint gives you a Southside, not a Basil Smash.

name: Gin Basil Smash
description: Gin, lemon and a whole handful of basil, shaken until it turns grass-green.
creator: Jörg Meyer
